units.text: The Engine Under Every Sport
Built, then measured.

A fair question stops a lot of parents before they book: how does getting faster in a gym make my kid better at their actual sport?
Here's the honest answer. Every sport skill rides on top of one engine, how much force a kid puts into the ground, how fast, how explosively. A great swing or a sharp cut still has to be powered by something. Train the engine and you don't make them better at one drill. You make them better at every move the sport asks for.
That's what our Multi-Sport Foundation Program develops. A bigger engine is a first step that beats the defender to the ball, which turns into more plays made, until the kid who used to get there a beat late is the one arriving first.
The first step in is the Athlete Analysis. We run your athlete through the same timing gates and velocity trackers we use every session, and you walk out with their real sprint and jump numbers. Not a tryout. A data set.
Then the guarantee: +1 mph. +3 inches. 90 days. Or we keep training them free.

A fair question stops a lot of parents before they book: how does getting faster in a gym make my kid better at their actual sport?

The swing, the cut, the first step to the ball, all of it has to be powered by something underneath it. A perfectly coached skill on top of a weak engine still loses the race to the ball. That's why so much sport-specific work doesn't show up in games the way parents expect, the skill got sharper but the engine never changed.
That's the part our Multi-Sport Foundation Program develops. Not one sport's drills, the speed and power that every sport draws from.
And when the engine grows, it shows up everywhere at once. It's the first step that beats the defender to the ball, which turns into more plays made every game, which becomes the kind of tape a coach stops to watch, until the kid who used to arrive a beat late is the one getting there first.
One mom shared that her son built himself up with us the right way, and that the strength and speed carried all the way to a D2 college scholarship. The training was never sport-specific. It was the foundation every sport sat on.

How Training Transfers to Every Sport

The Engine Under Every Sport
Built, then measured.

A fair question stops a lot of parents before they ever book: how does getting faster and jumping higher in a gym actually make my kid better at baseball, or soccer, or whatever they play?
Here's the honest answer. Every sport skill rides on top of one engine. How much force a kid puts into the ground, how fast they put it there, how explosively. The swing, the crossover, the first step to a loose ball, all of it is powered by that engine underneath. A beautifully coached skill sitting on top of a weak engine still loses the foot race, still gets bodied off the ball, still arrives a half step late.
That's the piece most families never get told. They pour years into sport-specific coaching, sharpen the mechanics, refine the technique, and then can't understand why it doesn't show up in games. The skill got better. The engine never changed. And the engine is what the game actually runs on.
This isn't a knock on skill coaching, by the way. Skill work matters, and a kid needs it. It just can't do a job it was never built to do. You can't coach a kid into more force production with a clipboard, the same way you can't paint a car into going faster. Those are two different jobs, and almost nobody is doing the second one.
That second job is the only thing our Multi-Sport Foundation Program does. It runs on The Velocity Code™, and every session we build the real, measured speed and power that sits underneath every sport, then prove it's moving with numbers you can see.
And when that engine grows, it doesn't show up in one drill. It shows up everywhere at once. It's the first step that beats the defender to the ball. That turns into more plays made every single game. More plays become the kind of tape a coach actually stops to watch, until one season in, the kid who used to get there a beat late is the one arriving first, in every sport they play.
One mom shared what that looked like for her son. He built himself up here the right way, added real strength and speed, and it carried all the way to a D2 college scholarship. None of his training with us was sport-specific. It was the foundation his sport was built on.
The first step in is the Athlete Analysis. We run your athlete through the same Dashr timing gates and GymAware velocity trackers the NFL uses, and you leave with their real sprint time, real jump height, and a clear picture of where they stand. Not a tryout. A data set you get to keep. From there, the path into the Multi-Sport Foundation Program is simple.
Coach Graham Wilkerson built this. He's a CSCS, the same credential D1 and NFL strength coaches carry, and he trained NFL athletes Zack Martin, Ted Karras, and Nick Martin before adapting these principles for the developmental window where they matter most.

A fair question stops a lot of parents before they ever book: how does getting faster and jumping higher in a gym actually make my kid better at baseball, or soccer, or whatever they play?
Here's the honest answer. Every sport skill rides on top of one engine. How much force a kid puts into the ground, how fast they put it there, how explosively. The swing, the crossover, the first step to a loose ball, all of it is powered by that engine underneath. A beautifully coached skill sitting on top of a weak engine still loses the foot race, still gets bodied off the ball, still arrives a half step late.
That's the piece most families never get told. They pour years into sport-specific coaching, sharpen the mechanics, refine the technique, and then can't understand why it doesn't show up in games. The skill got better. The engine never changed. And the engine is what the game actually runs on.
This isn't a knock on skill coaching, by the way. Skill work matters, and a kid needs it. It just can't do a job it was never built to do. You can't coach a kid into more force production with a clipboard, the same way you can't paint a car into going faster. Those are two different jobs, and almost nobody is doing the second one.
That second job is the only thing our Multi-Sport Foundation Program does. It runs on The Velocity Code™, and every session we build the real, measured speed and power that sits underneath every sport, then prove it's moving with numbers you can see.
And when that engine grows, it doesn't show up in one drill. It shows up everywhere at once. It's the first step that beats the defender to the ball. That turns into more plays made every single game. More plays become the kind of tape a coach actually stops to watch, until one season in, the kid who used to get there a beat late is the one arriving first, in every sport they play.
